{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABaPeskA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhD1kM8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 59, "title": "Profile and optimize CI test execution without reducing hardware validation coverage", "body": "## Problem

The existing `Browser Pages` GitHub Actions workflow has grown from approximately 2–3 minutes to **25–42 minutes** as the independent Saturn hardware/guest validation suite expanded. This now materially slows every autonomous implementation → review → fix → CI → merge cycle. All current checks pass, but their execution cost is becoming a development bottleneck.

This Issue is to **investigate the causes, design a sound optimization, implement it and demonstrate a measurable improvement**. It is not a request to remove tests, sacrifice emulation correctness or only write a performance proposal.

## Expected outcome

Retain the **complete existing Rust, Wasm, browser, homebrew/media reproducibility and publish-safety coverage** while materially reducing normal GitHub Actions wall-clock latency. The implementer should choose the most effective minimal design after collecting per-stage and per-test evidence, rather than assuming a particular parallelization framework is necessary.

The result must remain fully executable and verifiable by an autonomous agent. **No human approval, manual browser checks, real Saturn hardware, personal BIOS/media, workflow-owner sign-off or subjective confirmation is a completion gate.**

## Context and reproduction

At the time of drafting, the latest `main` is `402f9e8c1a2819a1e2f52723c7674f133f470dde`. Relevant files:

- [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/.github/workflows/pages.yml) — one `build` job serially performs Rustup setup, ~90 Python media/fixture checks, native Rust checks, Wasm build/Clippy, Playwright install, browser checks and Pages artifact upload; a separate dependent `deploy` job publishes only on `main`.
- [`scripts/browser-smoke.mjs`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/browser-smoke.mjs) — a large integrated Playwright runner (~3,300 lines plus imported scenario modules) that sequentially awaits many hardware guest scenarios and UI/browser tests, largely sharing one Chromium instance and some common page state.
- [`scripts/build-web.sh`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/scripts/build-web.sh) and [`docs/setup.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/blob/main/docs/setup.md) — supported local/CI validation paths.

### Measured GitHub Actions baseline

Use job/step timestamps in each linked GitHub run, not guesses about which subsystem is slow. These are **elapsed times**, including setup and (for main runs) deployment; the exact runtime varies by GitHub-hosted runner and revision.

| Revision / run | Workflow elapsed | Rust check | Browser validation | Wasm build | Outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [2026-10-20 `dbd981b` main](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/39448563946) | ~3m00s | 14s | 30s | 1m45s | success |
| [2026-10-23 `ed39a35` main](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/39961015334) | ~15m23s | 3m14s | 10m19s | 1m09s | success |
| [2026-10-24 `cd887d6` main](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/40090468518) | ~25m20s | 5m30s | 17m58s | 1m09s | success |
| [2026-10-24 PR #58](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/40093236785) | ~42m07s | 9m14s | 30m47s | 1m40s | success |
| [2026-10-25 `402f9e8` main](https://github.com/takahirox/saturn-rust/actions/runs/40147912040) | ~33m16s | 7m07s | **24m05s** | 1m21s | success |

The last main run's browser stage consumes ~72% of the overall run. Actual Pages deployment took ~12 seconds; it is **not** the bottleneck. Native Rust validation is the secondary bottleneck. Reproducible fixture checks were only a few seconds. The existing browser runner has no per-scenario timings, so the specific slowest guest scenario(s) are **not yet known**.

### Scope of investigation

1. Instrument the existing steps and individual browser scenario groups. Distinguish browser launch/page setup, Wasm initialization, emulated hardware-clock guest execution, Playwright polling, network/media loading, and actual assertions; instrument native test binaries or relevant guest suites as needed.
2. Rank the largest contributors using repeatable measurements. Assess serial browser orchestration, isolated page/context reuse, independent suite sharding/parallelization, long-running guest loops, redundant full cold boot, excessive polling, duplicated setup, and native test profile/fixture generation. Confirm what is actually expensive before modifying the architecture.
3. Implement a **maintainable improvement** chosen from the evidence: independent Playwright shards/contexts/jobs or workers with bounded concurrency; safe sharing of once-built Wasm/assets; reuse of immutable fixtures; reducing redundant setup; faster native test harness execution where logically equivalent; or other verified approaches. Maintain state isolation and deterministic per-guest results. Parallelize native/browser jobs if the dependency graph and artifact handoff make that beneficial. Optimize for **critical-path wall-clock time**, not merely more concurrent CPU usage.
4. Avoid speculative frameworks/dependencies and large unrelated refactors. It is acceptable to keep a small sequential integration suite for genuinely state-dependent tests while moving independent scenarios into separately executable suites.

## Nonnegotiable safety and correctness constraints

- **No dropping, skipping, weakening or rewriting away existing assertions** merely for speed. Preserve native Rust, SH-2/68k/DSP/bus/device traces, Wasm/Canvas/AudioWorklet, all three homebrew/diagnostic discs, responsiveness, invalid input/media, reset/fault, input privacy, no copyrighted media, and GitHub project subpath checks. Test names/group membership can change with a demonstrably equivalent coverage inventory.
- Do not reduce emulated cycle counts, expected state, timeouts or checks just to make a benchmark pass; only shorten legitimately redundant work when equivalence is established by existing/new independent assertions. Preserve negative controls and reproducible fixture hashes, and document any necessary fixture changes.
- Each test scenario must either run and report its real assertions or fail the CI. Do not hide flakiness with unconditional retries, catch-and-ignore exceptions, blanket skips, `|| true`, hardcoded successful results, cache-dependent passes, or silent test omissions. Avoid running shared writable browser state concurrently unless isolation is proven.
- Preserve CI's security/privacy constraints: `web/` allowlist and Pages subpath, local-only BIOS/disc bytes, zero proprietary assets, lockfiles and exact Wasm bindgen matching. No browser data uploads, external runtime CDN or nonlocal backend.
- Preserve deployment behavior: PRs validate but never deploy; only successful current `main` can deploy; superseded PR jobs may cancel, main deployments must not be overtaken. If validation is separated into jobs, artifact upload/deploy must depend on all mandatory suites and deploy only the *actually tested* web build. Existing failures must still fail the PR/merge pipeline.
- Keep the normal `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native/Wasm Clippy, fixture reproducibility, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and `npm run test:browser` workflows usable. The browser command must continue to run the **complete** suite by default, not a fast subset.
- There must be **no human-only acceptance condition** or real-BIOS/physical-console/external GitWeave investigation blocker.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Baseline and diagnosis:** add low-overhead instrumentation that prints meaningful per-browser-group and native/CI step timings on success **and on failure**. Collect an actual baseline against the checked revision and record the slowest scenarios plus an evidence-based explanation of the critical path. Do not assert a cause solely from the total browser-step time.
- [ ] **Implemented speedup:** ship and document at least one substantial performance improvement addressing the measured critical path, with corresponding regression tests for the runner/shard/job wiring. A plan, an unexecuted flag or added timers alone does not resolve this Issue.
- [ ] **Quantified before/after:** report reproducible *before and after* wall-clock results (environment, machine/runner, revision, commands and run IDs when available). Aim for **at least ~30% shorter full-browser validation** and a **material improvement in end-to-end PR validation latency** against comparable baseline hardware, while preserving all tests. Use comparable repeated runs (prefer medians of ≥3 where feasible) to avoid single-run noise. If those targets cannot be met, demonstrate and explain the best verified improvement and the remaining bottleneck; do not fabricate or force an unreliable benchmark gate.
- [ ] **Full-suite parity:** produce a manifest/report or equivalent reviewable audit that identifies existing test groups, shows each still runs by default and is counted, and establishes no dropped assertions, skipped cases, hashes, or negative-control behavior. A missing shard or a crashed worker must fail the parent command and CI.
- [ ] **Isolation and determinism:** independently executable browser scenarios produce the same recorded guest/Canvas/audio/input results regardless of grouping, order or concurrency (with repeated runs); there are no cross-test resets, shared-page races, stale Wasm state, media/asset leaks, or unhandled promise rejections.
- [ ] **CI integrity:** all mandatory checks still gate final green status; PRs cannot deploy, `main` deploy remains correctly serialized and gated, all assets and private-media restrictions are preserved, and a deliberately failing representative assertion or shard propagates a nonzero failure. No GitHub-hosted performance measurement is required to be a strict flaky CI threshold.
- [ ] **Validation on final tree:** run and report `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the registered reproducibility checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, `cargo clippy --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`, and the **full** `npm run test:browser`. Run the actual PR GitHub Actions workflow and record results where the existing tooling permits; do not block on a human to read logs.
- [ ] **Documentation:** update `docs/setup.md` and appropriate CI/development docs with the new complete-suite command(s), profiling invocation, measured results, concurrency-resource bounds, known bottlenecks and rollback/debugging instructions. Clearly separate optimization/test orchestration from Saturn hardware emulation behavior.

## Optional validation

Compare runtime across multiple GitHub runner attempts and compare median/p90. Additional cache experiments, more CI sharding or low-level emulator performance tuning may be worthwhile only if measured gains justify their complexity; they are not mandatory in themselves. Future optimization can proceed separately from this Issue.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All mandatory coverage, workflow-safety checks and actual performance measurements must be completed **before merge** in local/CI environments. Do not require a user to inspect the live GitHub Pages site manually.
